description: Yellow diamond warning sign carrying a black elephant silhouette, posted on forested highway stretches.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Slim galvanised post carrying a flat square plate rotated forty-five degrees to stand as a diamond on its point, plate face bright yellow with a black border band following the diamond edge and a solid black elephant silhouette filling the centre, a smaller rectangular yellow supplementary plate mounted on the post directly below carrying black lettering reading the Thai line ระวังช้าง above a smaller roman line reading ELEPHANT CROSSING Materials: Bright yellow retroreflective sheeting gone chalky and slightly greened at the edges, solid black pictogram paint, galvanised post with rust at the ground line, insect and road spatter across the lower face.

Legend: this object is a SIGN, and its printed legend is part of the object, not an annotation on the photograph. Render every letter, numeral, pictogram, arrow and coloured band described above, exactly as described and nothing more. Thai script must be rendered as Thai script with correct glyph shapes, above the roman line where both are described. Lettering and pictograms lie flat on the sign face, sharp, high-contrast and correctly proportioned, and the face must stay legible despite the camera angle. Do not leave the face blank, do not substitute lorem or invented wording, and do not add any text that was not described.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no watermarks, no drop shadow, and no border around the photograph itself.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.92. 192/800 triangles, 2/2 draw calls, 2/3 materials, 2/3 unique geometries, one 22 KB atlas and one 512 px canvas. Turntable: 0 and 180 segmented and hole-free; 90 and 270 fall under the gate segmenter's 3.5% frame-coverage floor (an edge-on sign is a sliver), the same recorded limitation the fence panels carry, and are not a defect of the build.

featureReviews.evidence: Diamond 0.9 m across (0.636 m side, r 0.03) at y 1.2-2.1 and a 0.6 x 0.2 m supplementary plate at y 0.98-1.18, both as plain 33 mm trays with NO rim lip and the diamond's brackets narrowed to the 0.08 m post (fourth build, owner review 2026-09-03: the grey lips read as borders and the 0.56 m brackets poked past the diamond's sloping edges as horizontal slats). Bounds 0.9 x 2.1 x 0.134 against the corrected declaration 0.9 x 2.1 x 0.13.
Post 0.08 m square (42 px across two faces at 378 px/m) to 2.0 m; height 2.1 from the plate's 803 px (2.12 m) and the proxy's 1.9-2.05. One spine over both plates; holeviz 0/1/0/1 enclosed pixels.
featureReviews.notes: The post foot is built to the corrected declared height; the plate shows the whole prop with an empty bottom row.

featureReviews.evidence: Diamond rectified from apex/right/base/left (485,107) (662,362) (509,496) (323,263) into a 512 x 512 bounding box and the lower plate from (403,514) (591,578) (588,688) (407,614), composed in one 0.9 x 1.12 m atlas (22 KB); elephant silhouette and both legend lines at their own positions.
featureReviews.notes: Rectified from ~250-500 plate pixels across, so the lettering edge is the plate's own softness.

name: Elephant Crossing Sign
nameTh: ป้ายระวังช้าง
notes: The diamond-on-point plate is the warning sign proper and the elephant pictogram is a solid filled silhouette rather than an outline, which is what lets it read at highway distance and survive a low texture resolution. The small rectangular supplementary plate below carrying the wording is how these are actually posted on Thai highways, and it is part of this asset rather than a separate prop because the two are always mounted on one post. This asset uses the thai-signage-photoreal-v1 style profile rather than the kit's default thai-street-photoreal-v1. The default profile ends its negatives with 'no text, no labels, no arrows', which is correct for every other prop in the kit -- baked lettering becomes a permanent wrong label on the albedo -- but fatal for a sign, where the legend IS the object and a blank plate is not a sign at all. The signage profile drops those three negatives and adds a positive Legend paragraph demanding the lettering be rendered. Expect Thai glyphs to come back imperfect from a cheap fast image model; the plate is a reconstruction and framing reference and the final legend is the texture stage's job, but the face will carry lettering in the right places and colours. Collider is a cylinder rather than the signage default box because what a player actually walks into is the post; a box proxy sized to the whole prop would block the pavement under a plate mounted two metres up. Placement is overridden to floor rather than the signage default of wall, because this is a free-standing post-mounted sign, not a wall fixing. Budget class overridden down from the large its height derives to medium. Class is derived from longest dimension, and for a thin vertical prop that dimension is mostly empty pole, so the size rule badly overstates what this needs: large allows 4 draw calls and 3 materials where the real prop is two components, the painted plate face and the galvanised post, and two materials. Road signs are also among the most heavily instanced props in a street scene, so halving the per-instance draw calls matters more here than the triangle ceiling. No destruction groups. Height corrected 2.4 -> 2.1 and depth 0.08 -> 0.13 in the v2 rebuild (2026-09-02): the plate shows the whole prop -- diamond 340 px wide for 0.9 m (378 px/m), apex y 107 to the post foot y ~910 = 803 px = 2.12 m; proxy diamond 0.44-0.47 H gives 1.9-2.05 m. Post 0.08 m square (42 px across two faces at 378 px/m = 0.11 m visible).
